edges.effect_quant: This is one of the more consistent cancer-prevention signals in reproductive epidemiology: ever use of combined oral contraceptives is associated with lower ovarian-cancer risk, and longer use appears more protective.
edges.mechanism: Oral contraceptives reduce ovulatory cycling and likely lower repeated inflammatory and repair stress at the ovarian epithelium. The duration-response pattern seen in multiple analyses fits that ovulation-suppression model better than a chance observational artifact.
edges.summary: Among the v4 reproductive-endocrinology topics, this is one of the clearest. Across large pooled datasets, women who have used oral contraceptives tend to have lower ovarian-cancer risk than never-users, and the reduction generally deepens with longer duration of use.
edges.caveats: The magnitude of benefit varies by population and formulation era, and this protective effect must be weighed against other outcomes that can move in the opposite direction. Much of the strongest recent synthesis is still observational.
